tasks.title: Portable fail-closed hooks + doctor hook-health
tasks.objective: No hook command can silently fail to spawn again: both runtime hook files resolve their interpreter from PATH, forge doctor executes every registered hook command verbatim on every platform and goes red with a named fix when one cannot run, and scaffold/adopt/upgrade provably ship the portable form to clients.
acceptance_criteria: All 5 commands in .claude/settings.json and all 3 in .codex/hooks.json replace /usr/bin/python3 with "$(command -v python3 || command -v python)", keeping the $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/factory/scripts/<script>.py form intact — the literal factory/scripts/<name>.py token must survive because check_dual_runtime.check_hook_registration regex-extracts it (check_dual_runtime.py:324); event parity between the two files unchanged.

forge doctor gains a hook-health check (existing _check pattern, doctor.py:202): parse both hook files, execute each registered command verbatim via sh -c from the repo root with a synthetic harmless hook payload on stdin (a read-only Bash tool_use JSON) and a benign expected outcome; any command that cannot spawn or errors is a required red check naming the exact command and the fix (doctor --fix / install python3). Healthy repo on macOS/Linux/Git-Bash: green.
A subprocess-free fast variant (sibling of fast_status, doctor.py:220) reports hook interpreter resolution via shutil.which for later consumption by forge next (wiring is WIN-1.2, not this task).

Gate tests: doctor hook-health green on the healthy repo; red with named command when the interpreter cannot resolve (PATH-controlled test env); scaffolded (forge init) and upgraded (forge upgrade) targets carry the portable command in both hook files (assert file content, reusing existing init/upgrade test fixtures); check_dual_runtime stays green. No new literal-interpreter string assertions introduced.
Decision 0038 text refined if implementation reveals corrections; status stays proposed (human accepts later).
verify_commands: uvx --with pytest python3 -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q -k "hook_health or portable or dual_runtime"
tasks.reviewer_focus: The verbatim-execution check must not mutate state (payload must be read-only-shaped and hooks must treat it as such — pre_tool_use on a read-only Bash payload allows and writes nothing; session_start/stop hooks invoked with harmless stdin must not append to ledgers or emit context side effects; if a hook DOES write on any input, the check must use its dry/harmless path explicitly, never skip it silently). The factory/scripts token must survive in the new command strings or check_dual_runtime's protection silently vanishes. Windows semantics reasoned, not assumed: hooks run under Git Bash.

tasks.title: Windows remediation (doctor --fix) + forge next preflight + docs
tasks.objective: A Windows dev with a missing toolchain gets a green harness from the agent alone: doctor --fix installs Git-for-Windows/Python via winget with all elevation batched into one confirm, forge next surfaces doctor --fix as step 1 on a hook-broken Windows clone, and docs/windows.md records the supported path.
acceptance_criteria: doctor --fix on windows (_platform_name, doctor.py:334) detects missing Git-for-Windows / Python >=3.10 and installs via winget through run_quiet list-argv; elevation-requiring actions batched into ONE consolidated confirm; never touches ~/.codex/config.toml or any user-global file; non-Windows platforms unaffected.

phase.cmd_next: on Windows, the fast hook-health check (WIN-1.1) runs at the TOP of the preflight block (before open-signals, phase.py:38) and a broken clone prints doctor --fix as step 1; healthy clones and non-Windows output byte-identical to today.

docs/windows.md: supported path (Git for Windows + Git Bash), agent-handled remediation flow, WSL2 escape hatch, codex Windows sandbox rationale with upstream issue links; cross-referenced from docs/degraded-mode.md.

Gate tests: --fix planning/batching logic with installer calls faked (single-confirm invariant asserted); next-preflight ordering on a simulated broken state; real UAC path explicitly NOT CI-testable — verified once on the affected client's machine and recorded as functional evidence (plan Verify).
verify_commands: uvx --with pytest python3 -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q -k "windows_fix or preflight or hook_health"
tasks.reviewer_focus: forge next must stay fast (no subprocess in the preflight) and byte-identical off-Windows; winget argv assembled but faked in tests; single-confirm batching is the contract, not per-package prompts.

tasks.title: Codex sandbox seam via delegation + windows-latest CI
tasks.objective: Codex Windows sandbox config rides the delegation with zero user setup — through whichever seam the installed companion actually exposes — and windows-latest CI proves the lockout and hook-health behavior on Windows forever after.
acceptance_criteria: Seam verification FIRST (read-only, against the installed companion): does task accept config passthrough, or does its config store cover sandbox mode? Implement the highest available fallback from the approved plan: (1) launch_companion (delegate.py:952) appends platform-conditional flags recorded via existing argv+argv_sha256 evidence; (2) doctor --fix invokes the companion's own config surface; (3) forge defer add with trigger 'companion exposes sandbox config' + documented gap in docs/windows.md. The chosen seam is recorded as an assumption (forge plan assume).

New harness-only .github/workflows/windows-gates.yml: windows-latest, setup-python 3.11, runs the lockout gate-test subset plus doctor hook-health against the checked-out repo; NOT added to COPY_WORKFLOWS (no client shipping); scaffold-check branch-protection context untouched.

Gate tests: whichever seam landed is asserted (argv flags in delegations.jsonl evidence for fallback 1; config invocation for fallback 2; deferral row for fallback 3); windows-gates.yml existence and harness-only placement asserted.
Windows-incompatible tests in the CI subset carry named skip reasons; the lockout deny/allow tests themselves run on windows-latest — skipping them does not satisfy this criterion.
verify_commands: uvx --with pytest python3 -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q -k "sandbox_seam or windows_gates or lockout"
tasks.reviewer_focus: Companion is external — no forking, no version pinning games; the seam decision must be evidence-backed and recorded, not assumed. The CI job must not widen the client gate surface (COPY_WORKFLOWS untouched, scaffold-check context unchanged).
